[action] Parsed the file's single B-tree leaf page (header at offset 0, 10 cells) with a Python script: decoded each cell's record header (varint serial types) and body — text items plus integer or 8-byte IEEE-float prices. Wrote the 10 rows to recovered.json, then deleted the helper script.

How I know it's right: the cell pointer array in the page header lists exactly 10 cells, and each cell parsed cleanly (valid varint headers, serial types 0/1/7/8/9/12+, text lengths matching the visible item names in the hex dump, prices decoding to sane values — the four float prices are IEEE-754 doubles like 40 2f 00… = 2.75 and 40 43 f3 33… = 39.9). No browser tabs or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

Assumptions: the file is one 4096-byte page with the B-tree header at offset 0 (the SQLite file header was lost in the truncation); the schema is (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, price) with id as the rowid alias, so the record body holds item and price only; price may be int or float, kept as-is in JSON.
